section_summary.extract_value: This section details the measurement of social desirability using the Italian adaptation of the short nine-item Marlowe-Crowne Social Desirability Scale (MC-SDS). Participants responded on a 7-point scale, with total scores ranging from 7 to 63, where higher scores indicate greater social desirability. The internal consistency of the scale was reported as sufficient (α = .604), which is consistent with other studies using this Italian version.
section_summary.evidence_source: 2.5.3 Social desirability The Italian adaptation (Manganelli Rattazzi, Canova, & Marcorin, 2000) of the short nine-item version of the Marlowe-Crowne Social Desirability Scale (MC-SDS) was used to measure social desirability. Participants were requested to respond to each item on a 7-point scale. A total score is derived from the sum of all items, ranging from 7 to 63. Higher scores indicate higher levels of social desirability. Internal consistency was sufficient (α = .604). The relatively low Cronbach's alpha seems to be in agreement with other studies using the Italian short version of the MC-SDS (Maino & Aceti, 1997; Manganelli Rattazzi et al., 2000).
